drafted_from: tool:keep-by-its-rule's own row (its words, input schema and sample run) and what its sample run answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Put a wake declaration of yours on tool:keep-by-its-rule with {"rule": "<the id of your keep rule's row>"} and the schedule you want; switch it on. Each firing asks your engine to apply that rule: it destroys, restorable for the undo window, the records of the rule's kind that the rule's row says have expired.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes the id of a keep rule's row and hands it to the engine, which reads the row; it keeps no row itself.
instructions: 1. Make a keep rule: a row of kind record:keep-rule with enabled, keeps_kind (the kind of record to keep), expire_when (the formula engine's rule tree and its fields; the fact age_ms is how long ago a record's newest write was, in milliseconds), page (records one firing destroys) and walk (records one firing looks at, at least the page).
2. Declare a wake of yours on tool:keep-by-its-rule with the input {"rule": "<the row's id>"} and the schedule you want (every hour, every night); it stays off until you switch it on.
3. Edit the row to change what is kept; the next firing reads it again. Turn enabled off to stop the rule. A record destroyed stays restorable until the undo window ends.

worked_examples.title: Ask the engine to apply one keep rule on its own sample
worked_examples.hands_back: It answered {"said": "Asked the engine to apply the keep rule record:keep-rule:example in own-records."} and the engine's keep effect for that rule.
